items.note: S1.3.1 gives the exchange (X,Y)->(-Y,X) over triples and restoration of scratch wires, but calls all three stages forward invocations (the middle stage is the inverse schedule from Y to X, lines 731-733, 761-763) and gives none of h=100, the copy/gather/scatter/side-injection motif or the neighbour rule.
States that a common frame per gate commuting with pointwise gates gives D_out S D_in^{-1} with edge cost D_vD_u^{-1}, as in lines 804-817; the reason is carried only by the quote, with no sub-steps.

S1.3.3 says only that nested nondegenerate subspaces of an m-dimensional space make s<Wm. It omits the space F^{tensor 3}, the central wires losing h as the only decreasing edges, L=Ich, the budget Wm-2N+2L and L/N<1/2.

It has the endpoint difference I_m, the shear (H,D)->(H+D,D) on every role and s_b<W_b m. It omits the projection assignment (P_U at gates and sinks, -P_{U_a} at the X sources) and the value s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.

It gives phase frames C_U, edge differences as products of aI+bX_v kernels, C^{tensor m} on every role, and s_c<W_c m. It does not say that there is one kernel per orthonormal residual basis vector (the source of the count s_c), and it omits the formula s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c and the diagonal corrections.
Has s<Wm for both networks and s/W<m^tau, but never gives the deficits eta_b, eta_c, the value tau=sigma=1-2^{-50} or why L<N/2 forces the saving.

S1.1 matches the elementary stream lemma. S1.2's claim drops the condition that the offset is prepared in b^{O(1)} time (it is present only in the quote) and the coprimality conditions on the rational coefficients.
Both the factorization A=E_1 Pi E_2 with a ones and the cost of exactly a interchanges plus O(V) are stated faithfully. No elimination argument is given.

S2.3 with S2.1-S2.2 follows the paper's route: role-stream split, edges done by recursive interchanges, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), O(Ve^tau). It omits that the network yields the shear H<-H+D, which three updates D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D turn into the interchange, and it omits the fixed-tape schedule and the row-field divisibility by W^k.
Gives O(Vu^tau) for arbitrary u-bit fields via high digits as rows and padding. It omits the split of the remaining width into base-m pieces, so it is not credited as derived.

Has H_0=bSCS, H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D and s_c child calls on f=e/m axes plus binary basis changes. It omits the conjugation by P_M that puts residual directions in coordinate slots and the inverse-child identity, and S3.1's 'D/m axes' ignores the e=m^k grouping.

Eight packed rotations with a restored third chunk, deterministic repair of an exponentially small exceptional set, and O(V(L^tau+1)) in the parameter family all match. The explicit delta_bad is not given.
S3.3 alludes to a recursion with children of volume V/W and ratio below m, but gives no recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), no leaves, no q_0 row chunks and no summation to O(d^{lambda'}).

The statement (Q_p(Hz), error below sqrt2 2^{-p}, O(Vd^{lambda'}), exact Gaussian dyadics with one truncation) is right, and the method follows the paper's route. The essential recurrence and its unrolling are not given, and the guard-width bound Delta is not quantified.

Gives the retained layout and the cost O(Tp[dK+pK^{tau-1}+l d^{lambda'}]). It omits the exact counterparts LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}, character cancellation, the bit-reversed order and the error bound.
Evaluation at a power of two, the established multiplier, centred residues and O(rp log(rp)) all match lines 3221-3262.

The route (two forward transforms in common LB order, pointwise products, opposite transform) and the error sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p} match. The plan omits the final exact scaling by M, the normalization identity and the error propagation, and it gives no cost.
The identity P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA, its time and the tensor form are stated. The plan omits the hypothesis theta=t/s-1>p/alpha^4, the definitions of P_s and P_t, and the error bound p^2.
Gives QF_t u = abar.(a*(abar.u))/T and says R cancels. It omits the chirp's definition, the explicit identity with (u*v)/S^2, and the conjugation that yields RF^+.
b, p, d, K, T and the axes match. 'Primes just below t_i' loosens the window (1-2eta)t_i<s_i<=(1-eta)t_i, and the plan omits the fixed rational exponents (other than kappa), alpha and gamma.
Phi is named and reduction to distinct prime axes is mentioned, but neither the map x->prod x_i^{mu_i} nor the triangular digit form is given.
S6.3 describes twisting the last coordinate into the ring without the map x_d->zeta y or the wrap check that makes it an isomorphism.

The source-transform composition (A, chirp convolution, B_0, 2^gamma, conjugation for the opposite sign) and the six algorithm steps with the scales S and 2^{2b+4}S match. Only the input scaling 2^{-b-2} is not given.
States error below 1/2, exact rounding and carries, but gives none of the error chain (E_s, E_w, 448b 2^{-3b/4}) or the role of gamma<=b/4 and p=6b.
Normalization by Tp, seven powers at most 1-2kappa, polylog absorption and the final bound match. The plan does not list the seven terms or the binding margin g_2=epsilon c(1-tau)=2kappa.
No step discusses the n log n conjecture or the liminf negation.

errors.says: Three stages of forward invocations realize (X,Y)->(-Y,X).
errors.paper: Stage 1 is a forward invocation X to Y, stage 2 the inverse forward schedule from Y to X (X<-X-Y), stage 3 forward again.

errors.says: s/W calls on role streams of volume V/W.
errors.paper: There are s child calls, each on a role stream of volume V/W; s/W is the normalized factor after dividing by V.

errors.says: The network turns C^{tensor D} into s_c calls on D/m axes.
errors.paper: The recursion acts on groups of e=m^k chunks (s calls on e/m chunks each), after the first q_0 chunks are used as rows and D-q_0 is split into base-m pieces.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route from the network (S1.3) to the interchange (S2) and the butterfly layer (S3), then through transforms, resampling and the algorithm to the cost bound (S7). It thins at the source of the saving. S1.3.3 asserts s<Wm without the labels' dimension budget Wm-2N+2L, the loss L=Ich or L/N<1/2. The exponent tau=1-2^{-50} is never derived, and the layer recurrence (S3.3) appears without its formula or its unrolling to d^{lambda'}.

steps.note: The exchange (X,Y)->(-Y,X) over triples and scratch restoration are there, but h=100, N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3 are not; m is used without definition.
Common frame per gate, commuting with pointwise gates, giving D_out S D_in^{-1} and edge costs D_vD_u^{-1}.
Nested nondegenerate subspaces of an m-dimensional space are named, but not F^{tensor 3} or that the central wires from time 3 to 4, each losing h, are the only decreasing edges.
S1.3.3 links nested labels to edge-difference ranks but never says rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U or that the N rank-one source edges are exceptions.
No step gives sum |Delta dim| = Wm-2N+2L, L=Ich or s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
s<Wm is asserted, but L/N=100/539 or 101/539 <1/2 and the deficit N-2L>0 that produce it are missing.
S1.3.4 has endpoint difference I_m, so every role undergoes (H,D)->(H+D,D). The projection assignment is missing, but the identity and its role are present.
E_1 Pi E_2 factorization, exactly a interchanges plus O(V) for a rank-a shear, and edges done by smaller interchanges giving s calls in the recurrence.

Row-split streams, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) and s/W<m^tau giving O(Ve^tau) are present. The exponent tau=1-2^{-50} and its derivation from eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20 are absent, so this is graded conservatively.

central.summary: The plan reconstructs the outer mechanism of the saving: frames (C2), the endpoint identity and shear (C7), and edges as recursive calls (C8), with the recurrence shape in place. It does not reconstruct why s<Wm: the labels, rank-equals-dimension-change, the budget Wm-2N+2L and L/N<1/2 (C3-C6) are named or absent. The explicit exponent tau=1-2^{-50} is never obtained.
